detail.body:
## Overview

Enabling fp8 attn for fp8 KV cache for hardware-capable AMD GPUs, a new PR to replace stale #37973.

## Claims
`TRITON_ATTN` backend is still being used for multimodal models(Gemma3, Gemma4 etc) as both `ROCM_ATTN` and AITER don't have this support.

This flag enablement should be safe; later in attention.py https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bb87d227d4b964abb2a966cdf9194f3d376d9bbe/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py#L469
`self.kv_cache_dtype.startswith("fp8")` explicitly checks if the quantization is fp8.

## Validation
paraphrasing from user feedback: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5683
**Setup.** Single Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201). Model `gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic`, `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `cudagraph_mode FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1`. 

| | prefill, cache-missing 7.7K prompt | decode | 
|---|---|---|
| before | 1102 tok/s (1102–1103) | 33.38 (33.35–33.42) |
| **this PR** | **4574 tok/s (4564–4585)** | **36.08 (36.04–36.12)** |
| speedup | **4.15x** | **+8.1%** |



## Details
`ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` backend has enabled fp8 fast attn, and this PR brings it to parity after #57750

TODO: currently the `supports_fp8()` functions uses:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/dac35c5b66efb0ddabb6f67af5d1817b2c74edc0/vllm/platforms/rocm.py#L1082
Not sure that is accurate for all CDNA GPUs.

---

@@ -46,16 +46,17 @@
 def _fp8_reload_unsupported() -> bool:
     """Whether the FP8 reload/online-quantize tests should be skipped.
 
-    ``supports_fp8()`` returns True on MI250 (gfx90a) because the general
-    quantization paths upcast FP8 weights, but gfx90a has no native FP8 and
-    cannot run these reload models, so treat it as unsupported here.
+    ``supports_fp8()`` returns True on MI250 (gfx90a) and RDNA3 (gfx11)
+    because the general quantization paths upcast FP8 weights, but neither has
+    native FP8 and cannot run these reload models, so treat them as
+    unsupported here.
     """
     if not current_platform.supports_fp8():
         return True
     if current_platform.is_rocm():
-        from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx90a
+        from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx11, on_gfx90a
 
-        return on_gfx90a()
+        return on_gfx90a() or on_gfx11()
     return False

@@ -559,6 +559,11 @@ def __init__(
         self.use_alibi_sqrt = use_alibi_sqrt
         self.chunk_lookback = chunk_lookback
         self.supports_quant_query_input = current_platform.is_cuda()
+        if current_platform.is_rocm():
+            # Enable GPUs with fp8 MMA support
+            from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx11, on_gfx90a
+
+            self.supports_quant_query_input = not (on_gfx90a() or on_gfx11())
 
         self._kv_quant_mode = get_kv_quant_mode(kv_cache_dtype)
         self._is_per_token_head_quant = self._kv_quant_mode.is_per_token_head

For sure I will not enable it on gfx90a because there is guaranteed to have no benefit. My original goal was to at least enable this for gfx1201, as we have users reporting this can improve prefill performance a lot. I don't work with gfx942, gfx950 or gfx1250; and I can't do any testing. I am happy to leave them untouched/enable together based on reviwers' preference. 

Another concern I had was we have inconsistent behaviors in AMD backends. `TRITON_ATTN` and `ROCM_ATTN` both disable query quantization, whereas `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` enables it. I personally feel we should have consistent settings in all of AMD's attention backends, or made clear to the users for them to pick whether to sacrifice accuracy for performance.

> > I was thinking to put gfx90a to return False for `supports_fp8()`, but that will break
> > https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/385d86a6cf6f05051899b53d83ec55c63cccb379/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py#L157
> > 
> > so any fp8-moe models can't be used.
> > I can stay off from the `supports_fp8()` API to avoid breaking other usecases. if `enable = not on_gfx11() and not on_gfx90a()` is not too untidy. Meanwhile using this API in AITER attn is probably fine, because gfx90a is not supported there.
> 
> How is this run on machine supported by non-fp8 machine? Does the aiter moe kernel perform dequantization on the fly?

Yes, exactly. The Triton compiler does this behind the scene when using `tl.dot()`, for GPUs that doesn't support fp8 MMA. The `supports_fp8()` function is used at model load time, so its closest meaning is "is this fp8 model runnable on this GPU".

Thus, that function shouldn't be used in this case. I made the change and also added gfx11 to `supports_fp8()` to match the desired behaviour. This enables gfx11 to run fp8 MOE models. (TRITON dequantizes on the fly like gfx90a)

---

```
---
To summarize, in this PR I intend to:
1. enable fp8 moe models on gfx11
2. enable query quantization on gfx1201(potentially CDNAs based on your preference). I can run other accuracy tests other than `lm_eval` + `gsm8k` if you can provide me the commands

Appreciate further feedbacks. @tjtanaa

  --port 8000

lm_eval (chat template, full 1319, 5-shot, greedy):
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "model=/mnt/nas_share/models/google/gemma-4-12B-it,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,timeout=600,tokenizer=/home/user/eval_fp8_triton_q/gemma4_tok,max_gen_toks=512" \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --fewshot_as_multiturn \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --use_cache /home/user/eval_fp8_triton_q/cache_main_chat \
  --output_path /home/user/eval_fp8_triton_q/main_chat \
  --log_samples
```
pinging @JartX for: enabling fp8 MOE models on gfx11. I know it's not ideal to use such models; users should either use unquantized/w4a16, but this PR gives basic support instead of hard failure.

Thanks for the ping! Getting FP8 MoE checkpoints to load on gfx11 instead of failing outright sounds good to me, even if W4A16 or bf16 is still the better choice there.

I went through the supports_fp8() callers on main and the change stays fairly contained. The Triton MoE path is the one that actually changes, and the torch scaled-mm kernels keep their own gfx11 exclusion. One thing worth knowing: on gfx11 the linear layers only have a kernel for block-scaled FP8 (TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel). As far as I can tell, a per-channel "FP8-Dynamic" MoE would still fail, just in the linear layers instead of the MoE. Mentioning "block FP8" in the description would set the right expectations.

Small side effect: the torchao Float8-activation check also relies on supports_fp8(), so on gfx11 users would now get torchao's internal assertion instead of our clearer error.

One more thing: since you have the W7900s, could you run `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8` on gfx1100 with a full GSM8K (no `--limit`)? It's block FP8 and a GDN hybrid, so it would cover the MoE path and the hybrid layers on a dGPU in one go. With that I'd be happy to approve the gfx11 side. I'll leave the query-quant part to @tjtanaa, since I can't test CDNA.

Ran `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8`(text only) full 1319 gsm8k on gfx1151:
```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --port 8000

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "model=$M,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,timeout=600,tokenizer=$M,max_gen_toks=512" \
  --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
  
  
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9591|±  |0.0055|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9583|±  |0.0055|
  ```

This model is tight to fit on single gfx1100. Used single gfx1151 instead to avoid tensor parallel complexity, and saved multiGPU gfx1100 server for #52970.

You are right perChannel fp8 gemm support is missing in upstream now. This PR only unblocks moe checkpoint load, as we are fully capable in the moe path. There is separate PR enabling perChannel fp8 gemm in aiter: #60672

@JartX
